subject: Cascading 5xx wave — FastRetail escalation and action plan
messages:
From: Lisa Park <lisa.park@fastretail.com>

Cc: FastRetail SRE <sre@fastretail.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: High error rates and timeouts — urgent help needed

Monica —

We started seeing a sharp increase in 5xx/429 errors and client timeouts affecting checkout flows at ~08:40 PST. This is impacting ~12% of traffic and causing payment failures for some customers. Our SRE team captured attached traces and sampling of request headers (fastretail-logs-1205.zip).

We opened a PagerDuty incident (PDR-82419) and are preparing a customer incident page. Can Redwood confirm whether this is an internal retry amplification / autoscaler issue or something on our side? We need an immediate mitigation plan and a statement for our execs.

Requested:
- Immediate mitigation steps you are taking (rate-limits, fallback model, capacity bump)
- ETA for stabilization and estimated customer impact
- Whether Redwood will consider credits for impacted traffic (pending root cause)

Thanks,
Lisa Park
Head of Platform Reliability
FastRetail

Forwarding Lisa's note — putting this on priority. Quick summary: customer reports ~12% 5xx/429 spike starting ~08:40 PST; checkout failing; PagerDuty incident open. Attaching their logs.

Immediate ask: can SRE/infra confirm whether we are seeing a retry amplification pattern or autoscaler lag on inference clusters for their region? If so, we should push emergency throttles and a model fallback while we stabilize.

- Emergency client-side throttles (configurable rate-limit on FastRetail route)
- Pin a lower-size model or turn on prefix-KV cache warmup for their tenant
- Manual capacity increase / prioritize bursts for their Dedicated pool if possible
- Exec communication: draft note to FastRetail execs + proposed credits if root cause on Redwood

I will coordinate customer comms once we have confirmed actions.

Thanks — Monica

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: monica.patel@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-05T09:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: High error rates and timeouts — FastRetail (urgent triage)

Monica / team — quick triage notes after sampling the attached bundle: 
- Observed pattern: client retries with low backoff jitter + upstream 5xx responses -> amplified load on model pods (retry amplification).
- Autoscaler behavior: we see scale-up attempts but warm-up latency for large models (KV cache not populated) contributes to high tail latency -> more client retries.
- Error mix: ~60% 5xx from model worker OOM/backpressure, ~40% 429 from per-tenant queuing/throttles hitting limits under surge.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (fast, reversible):
1) Apply temporary per-tenant request-rate cap for FastRetail on edge (reduce retry loop) — config change, low risk, immediate effect.
2) Force-fallback their route to a smaller quantized model variant for the next 30 minutes to remove heavy warm-up costs.
3) Enable aggressive KV cache prefill for their prefix patterns (warmup job) while scale completes.
4) If needed, increase Dedicated pool burst capacity (request sent to infra ops).

I attached the SRE triage checklist for steps we've performed. I'll start the fallback and rate-cap now unless objections.

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: sre-triage-checklist.pdf

Lisa —

Thanks again for the quick signal and the logs. We ran the mitigations Rishi recommended: emergency per-tenant rate cap, temporary fallback to a smaller quantized model, and KV cache prefill. Infra also applied a short burst increase to the Dedicated pool. Those steps reduced 5xx/429 rates to baseline within ~22 minutes of the initial mitigation.

Next steps we are executing now:
- Postmortem (owner: Markus) is being drafted. We'll include timeline, root cause (retry amplification + autoscaler warm-up + alerting gaps), and concrete remediation items (new runbook for tenant emergency throttles, SLO re-calibration for tail latency, autoscaler tuning for faster warm-up, and improved alert thresholds).
- Credit proposal: Attached is a comp offer we will discuss in the exec call. We are open to agreeing credits if our postmortem confirms Redwood responsibility.
- Exec call: can we schedule a 30-minute call this afternoon at 4:30 PT to walk your execs through what happened and our remediation plan?

Apologies for the disruption — we take incidents like this seriously. I will follow up with the postmortem draft and timeline by tomorrow EOD.

Best regards,
Monica Patel
